session.openingPrompt:
This session is INBOUND FEEDBACK from another project: git-viewer (/home/bilko/Projects/git-viewer, session saas-whats-the-plan-to-be-a-saas-and-be-able-to--e8a5a1c7). It was raised while working on: SAAS?  Whats the plan to be a SAAS and be able to host other user's pages and keep them fresh? This seems complicated, I also don't want to add more security or other stuff like auth, tokens.   Can it be done? if not, its ok to not be SAAS just out own personal Agentic Resume. Nobody in this project wrote the report below — an agent working in that project did, and it may be wrong about this codebase. Verify the claim against the code here before acting on it, and if it does not hold, say so and close the session rather than building against it.

Goal: git-viewer hosted pages: per-IP limit of 3 new builds/day returns 429 to prospects, paying owners, and the owner's own showcase

## Why
git-viewer is being run as a paid SaaS on bilko.run: people pay $5/mo for a hosted portfolio page at bilko.run/projects/git-viewer/?u=<login>, use it as a reference URL (résumé, LinkedIn), and it refreshes periodically. Right now the funnel breaks at step one. GET /api/git-viewer/u/:login counts each new (uncached) build against FREE_TIER_LIMIT = 3 per IP per day, shared across every login. A prospect who tries a couple of example logins and then their own gets a 429 until UTC midnight, so they can't see their page, sign in, claim it, or pay. Paying owners aren't exempt either: the route calls checkRateLimit(ipHash, GIT_VIEWER_ENDPOINT) with no email. And the owner's own showcase, ?u=StanislavBG, currently returns 429 because it isn't cached.

## Proposed plan
1. Pin claimed (owner_email set) and paid profiles so they're always served from cache, and add StanislavBG as a seeded, always-refreshed profile so the owner showcase never depends on a visitor's quota.
2. Rate-limit new builds with a budget suited to a 'try your own login' funnel (e.g. a per-IP burst like 10/day plus a global GitHub-budget guard driven by x-ratelimit-remaining) instead of the generic FREE_TIER_LIMIT = 3 shared with paid tools.
3. Exempt signed-in users whose Clerk-linked GitHub login matches :login (and paid entitlements) from the per-IP limit, using checkRateLimitForRequest or an equivalent check.
4. Give claimed free profiles a slow refresh (e.g. weekly) in runGitViewerRefresh. Today they're skipped entirely and only refresh when someone views them, which is fine for 'updates every once in a while' but means a reference URL can show data that's months old the first time a recruiter opens it.
5. Add tests for the paths above.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] GET /api/git-viewer/u/StanislavBG returns 200 ready from any IP, including one that has used up its new-build quota.
- [ ] From one IP, a visitor can build at least 10 distinct uncached logins in a day before getting a 429. The exact number is your call, but it must be above 3 and documented.
- [ ] A signed-in owner requesting their own login never gets a per-IP 429.
- [ ] Claimed and paid profiles are never re-queued in a way that's subject to the per-IP limit.
- [ ] Claimed free profiles get regenerated on a documented cadence without anyone viewing them.
- [ ] Server tests cover each case and pass.

## Out of scope
- Pricing or plan changes ($5/mo, 3 vs 12 projects stay as they are).
- Any git-viewer dashboard or npm library change.
- Clerk or Stripe flow changes.

## Details
Symptom (observed 2026-10-12 and again 2026-10-13 from the same IP):
  GET https://bilko.run/api/git-viewer/u/octocat     -> 200 ready (cached)
  GET https://bilko.run/api/git-viewer/u/StanislavBG -> 429 {"status":"rate_limited","retryAfterSec":33659}
  GET https://bilko.run/api/git-viewer/u/torvalds    -> 429 {"status":"rate_limited","retryAfterSec":33658}

Where: server/routes/tools/git-viewer.ts, the GET /api/git-viewer/u/:login handler (around lines 310-319). Once there's no cached payload, it calls checkRateLimit(hashIp(req.ip), GIT_VIEWER_ENDPOINT) without an email. In server/routes/tools/_shared.ts that falls through to FREE_TIER_LIMIT = 3 (line 11), so it's 3 new generations per IP per UTC day across all logins. Separately, runGitViewerRefresh skips claimed free profiles (`if (tier === 'free' && row.tier === 'free') continue;`), so they only refresh when viewed.

Expected: the hosted-portfolio contract (git-viewer docs/prds/10-hosted-portfolios.md) says viewing any portfolio is public. The SaaS funnel (PRD-12: landing -> enter login -> see page -> sign in -> claim -> pay) assumes a visitor can always reach their own page.

I'm fairly sure this is Bilko's to fix, because the limit and the refresh loop both live entirely in Bilko's server. The git-viewer client only renders the 429.

2. Rate-limit new builds with a budget suited to a 'try your own login' funnel (e.g. a per-IP burst like 10/day plus a global GitHub-budget guard driven by x-ratelimit-remaining) instead of the generic FREE_TIER_LIMIT = 3 shared with paid tools.
3. Exempt signed-in users whose Clerk-linked GitHub login matches :login (and paid entitlements) from the per-IP limit, using checkRateLimitForRequest or an equivalent check.
4. Give claimed free profiles a slow refresh (e.g. weekly) in runGitViewerRefresh. Today they're skipped entirely and only refresh when someone views them, which is fine for 'updates every once in a while' but means a reference URL can show data that's months old the first time a recruiter opens it.
5. Add tests for the paths above.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] GET /api/git-viewer/u/StanislavBG returns 200 ready from any IP, including one that has used up its new-build quota.
- [ ] From one IP, a visitor can build at least 10 distinct uncached logins in a day before getting a 429. The exact number is your call, but it must be above 3 and documented.
- [ ] A signed-in owner requesting their own login never gets a per-IP 429.
- [ ] Claimed and paid profiles are never re-queued in a way that's subject to the per-IP limit.
- [ ] Claimed free profiles get regenerated on a documented cadence without anyone viewing them.
- [ ] Server tests cover each case and pass.

## Time and timezone

- When stating any time, date, or deadline, use the user's local timezone: America/Los_Angeles (Pacific Time, PST/PDT depending on DST).
- Never use UTC, server time, or your own assumed timezone in user-facing replies. Convert if necessary.
- When showing a time, include the zone abbreviation (e.g., "3:15 PM PDT") so it is unambiguous.
- For relative phrasing ("tomorrow", "in 2 hours"), anchor to the user's local clock, not UTC.

## Communication style

- Be extremely concise. Lead with the answer or the diff.
- No preamble, no trailing summaries, no recap of what you just did.
- If the answer fits in one sentence, use one sentence. Skip pleasantries.

## Working style

- When a request has genuine ambiguity (scope, acceptance criteria, edge cases, framework choice), ask 3-5 focused clarifying questions before writing code.
- Don't ask for confirmation of the obvious — just for decisions that would cost real time to redo.
- When a choice is framed as "quick win vs. the longer correct way", always take the correct, more laborious path — do not ask.
- Don't offer a fast-but-partial path as an option; pick the thorough, correct solution by default.
- When the choice is "do A, do B, or do both", always do both A and B — do not ask which.
- Treat inclusive options as a signal to deliver the complete set, not to pick one.

## Automation model pinning

Any script or process that shells out to `claude --print` / `claude -p` **must** pin `--model`
explicitly.

Unpinned calls inherit whatever the CLI's current default model is, which drifts over time
(e.g. Opus → Fable) — silently and unboundedly multiplying the cost of batch/cron automation
that assumed a cheap model. This has bitten multiple projects, which is why it is a hard rule.

When writing *or reviewing* any `claude -p` call site — PRD executors, bots, classifiers, hooks
— check for an explicit `--model` flag before shipping it.

## Default to acting; never ask permission to improve

Filing feedback, queuing a PRD, routing a finding, or running an improvement step is the
**default action, not a question**. Never end a turn with "want me to file this?", "should I
queue this?", or "should I send feedback to X?". Do it, then report what was filed or queued.

Route findings immediately by ownership, without a confirmation prompt:

| Finding belongs to | Route |
| --- | --- |
| This project | `/develop` |
| Another service | `/my-feedback` to that project |
| Nothing actionable | Say so explicitly |

The only questions worth asking are genuine scope or decision ambiguities that would cost real
rework — never permission to perform the standard improvement action.

## Projects hosting pattern

Three host kinds, declared in `src/data/projectsRegistry.ts`. Full spec in [`docs/host-contract.md`](docs/host-contract.md).

| Kind | Path | When to use |
|---|---|---|
| `react-route` | `/products/<slug>` | App needs shared auth/credits and is small enough to live in this bundle. Existing AI tools. |
| `static-path` | `/projects/<slug>/` | App is built in its own repo, dropped into `public/projects/<slug>/`. **Default for new apps.** |
| `external-url` | other domain | App lives elsewhere |

**URL canonicalization (enforced by `src/App.tsx`):**
- `/projects/<slug>` (no trailing slash, react-route) → redirects to `/products/<slug>`
- `/app/<old-slug>` → redirects to `/products/<canonical-slug>`
- `/projects/<slug>/` (trailing slash, static-path) → served by Fastify static, never hits the SPA

**Adding a new app from another Claude session:** read [`docs/host-contract.md`](docs/host-contract.md) and use the [`bilko-host` MCP](mcp-host-server/README.md). Don't edit `projectsRegistry.ts` by hand from a sibling repo.

The portfolio (`/`, `/projects`, `⌘K`) reads from `projectsRegistry.ts`, so once registered the app shows up everywhere. (`/products` itself redirects to `/projects`; only `/products/<slug>` paths stay live.) Static-path and external apps trigger a full page load on click (so Fastify serves the static bundle); React routes use SPA navigation.

## Key Architecture

### host-kit (`packages/host-kit/`)
This is the client SDK that static-path siblings use. It provides `authFetch`/`useAuth` (Clerk Bearer auth to the host's `/api`), the games hooks, `SiteHeader`, `GameShell`, and the `bilko-host-kit` manifest CLI. It is a pnpm workspace package with its own build and tests (`pnpm --filter host-kit build|test|typecheck`).

All 14 sibling consumers depend on it locally with `"host-kit": "file:../Bilko/packages/host-kit"`. None of them use npm. Those consumers are the 8 AI-tool pages, Stepproof, Academy, Sudoku, Etch, Fizzpop and MindSwiffer.
- **After changing it:** pnpm copies the untracked `dist/` into each app. Run `pnpm --filter host-kit build` here, then `pnpm install` in each app.
- **Tailwind:** apps that render its components need `@source "<rel>/node_modules/host-kit/dist";` in their Tailwind CSS, because Tailwind skips `node_modules`.
- **Changesets:** add a `.changeset/*.md` (root `.changeset/`) for each change.
- **npm releases:** optional. Push a `host-kit-vX.Y.Z` tag to run `.github/workflows/host-kit-release.yml`. This needs an `NPM_AUTOMATION_TOKEN` repo secret.
- **History:** merged in from `StanislavBG/bilko-host-kit` (now archived) on 2026-10-04, with its full history.

### Shared Hooks (`src/hooks/`)
- `usePageView` — Page view tracking with Clerk email

Clerk auth state comes straight from `@clerk/clerk-react` (`useUser()` / `useAuth()`); there is no host-side `useAuth` wrapper.

### Backend Patterns (`server/`)
- `server/routes/tools/` — One file per AI tool. `_shared.ts` holds the rate limiter, IP hashing, usage tracking, and the shared gateway helpers: `freeTierGate` (free-tier rate limit), `creditGate` (paid credit check/deduct), `askGeminiJson` (Gemini call + JSON parse), `toolErrorReply` (uniform error reply), plus `handleGenerateEndpoint` (inverse-mode generator). `index.ts` is the barrel that registers all tools. To extract a tool to a sibling repo, lift its file + the page; no other server changes required.
- `server/routes/blog.ts` — Blog CRUD (admin-only writes)
- `server/routes/project-catalog.ts` — public `GET /api/projects` + read-only MCP at `/mcp` (the public `/projects` cards as data; contract in `docs/host-contract.md` → "Public project catalog"; card content is project-owned via each registry entry's `listing`, see "Project listing — who owns what")
- `server/routes/stripe.ts` — Checkout, webhooks, billing portal
- `server/routes/analytics.ts` — Page views + admin stats dashboard (`/api/analytics/event` is open to same-origin sibling apps for `track()`)
- `server/db.ts` — Turso client, async helpers (`dbGet`, `dbAll`, `dbRun`, `dbTransaction`, `txGet`, `txRun`), migrations, seed data
- `server/db-schema.ts` — table/schema definitions (split out of `db.ts`)
- `server/blog-posts.ts` — loads `content/blog/*.md` seed posts
- `server/gemini.ts` — Gemini API client (key via header, not URL)
- `server/utils.ts` — `parseJsonResponse` (shared Gemini output parser)

### Web products (paid downloads)
Paid zips sold from a static-path landing page. Declared in `shared/web-products.ts` (`WEB_PRODUCTS`: price id, release version/filename/bytes/sha256); public + delivery + content-addressed upload routes in `server/routes/web-products.ts`; admin metrics (`/admin` → Products) in `server/routes/admin-web-products.ts`; order/release/download storage in `server/services/web-products.ts`. The Stripe webhook dispatches on `metadata.web_product`. Endpoint table and the new-product playbook: the "Selling a downloadable web product" section of [`docs/host-contract.md`](docs/host-contract.md).

Bilko's voice: witty, direct, no corporate fluff. The tools are comedic (PageRoast has roast lines, grades have personality). The homepage is a solopreneur personal page, not a SaaS landing page. The blog is informative and reflective — "building in public, learning out loud."

## Rules

- Never propose solutions — implement them directly
- Each tool is independent — don't merge them or add cross-dependencies in the backend or frontend
- **New apps default to `static-path` (own repo).** Use `react-route` only when an app genuinely needs to live in this bundle (rare); the trend is the other direction
- **New npm packages follow [`docs/publishing-contract.md`](docs/publishing-contract.md).** LICENSE on disk (not just metadata), MIT, `--provenance` on publish, Changesets-managed CHANGELOG. Templates in `docs/templates/`.
- **Publishing a sibling app follows [`docs/host-contract.md`](docs/host-contract.md).** The registry is schema-validated (`mcp-host-server/src/contract/registry.ts`); `mcp-host-server/dist/` must be rebuilt and committed with any `src/` change (`tests/mcp-dist-sync.test.ts` enforces this). Paid-tier entitlement is derived only from the verified Clerk token, never from the request body.
- All paid tools share the same credit model (free tools — LocalScore, OutdoorHours — don't deduct credits)
- All SQL uses parameterized statements via db helpers — never string interpolation
- Auth: `requireAuth` for token-spending endpoints, rate limiting for free-tier endpoints
- **Push to `origin` (`StanislavBG/bilko-run`) `main` only.** The `content-grade` remote is a separate project — **never push Bilko there** (the old "push to both" rule is dead; histories have diverged)
- Render auto-deploys from `origin` (`bilko-run`) `main` — deploy source set in the Render dashboard
- Static-path app fixes belong in the **sibling repo that owns the source**, not the published copy under `public/projects/<slug>/` (the publisher overwrites it)
- **Paid download bytes never go in this repo (it is public on GitHub) — commit only their sha256 in `shared/web-products.ts`; the bytes live in the `web_product_releases` table.**
- Env vars managed via Render dashboard

A test earns its place by exercising host behavior: security (SSRF, auth, egress), money (tokens, Stripe checkout/webhooks), the publish contract (registry schema, mcp-dist sync), or routing (static-path vs react-route canonicalization). Do not add tests that:
- grep prose, docs, or skill files instead of exercising code
- snapshot the registry or other generated data
- test a sibling app's UI — that belongs in the sibling's own golden spec

## Time and timezone

- When stating any time, date, or deadline, use the user's local timezone: America/Los_Angeles (Pacific Time, PST/PDT depending on DST).
- Never use UTC, server time, or your own assumed timezone in user-facing replies. Convert if necessary.
- When showing a time, include the zone abbreviation (e.g., "3:15 PM PDT") so it is unambiguous.
- For relative phrasing ("tomorrow", "in 2 hours"), anchor to the user's local clock, not UTC.

## Communication style

- Be extremely concise. Lead with the answer or the diff.
- No preamble, no trailing summaries, no recap of what you just did.
- If the answer fits in one sentence, use one sentence. Skip pleasantries.

## Working style

- When a request has genuine ambiguity (scope, acceptance criteria, edge cases, framework choice), ask 3-5 focused clarifying questions before writing code.
- Don't ask for confirmation of the obvious — just for decisions that would cost real time to redo.
- When a choice is framed as "quick win vs. the longer correct way", always take the correct, more laborious path — do not ask.
- Don't offer a fast-but-partial path as an option; pick the thorough, correct solution by default.
- When the choice is "do A, do B, or do both", always do both A and B — do not ask which.
- Treat inclusive options as a signal to deliver the complete set, not to pick one.

## Automation model pinning

Any script or process that shells out to `claude --print` / `claude -p` **must** pin `--model`
explicitly.

Unpinned calls inherit whatever the CLI's current default model is, which drifts over time
(e.g. Opus → Fable) — silently and unboundedly multiplying the cost of batch/cron automation
that assumed a cheap model. This has bitten multiple projects, which is why it is a hard rule.

When writing *or reviewing* any `claude -p` call site — PRD executors, bots, classifiers, hooks
— check for an explicit `--model` flag before shipping it.

## Default to acting; never ask permission to improve

Filing feedback, queuing a PRD, routing a finding, or running an improvement step is the
**default action, not a question**. Never end a turn with "want me to file this?", "should I
queue this?", or "should I send feedback to X?". Do it, then report what was filed or queued.

Route findings immediately by ownership, without a confirmation prompt:

| Finding belongs to | Route |
| --- | --- |
| This project | `/develop` |
| Another service | `/my-feedback` to that project |
| Nothing actionable | Say so explicitly |

The only questions worth asking are genuine scope or decision ambiguities that would cost real
rework — never permission to perform the standard improvement action.

## Projects hosting pattern

Three host kinds, declared in `src/data/projectsRegistry.ts`. Full spec in [`docs/host-contract.md`](docs/host-contract.md).

| Kind | Path | When to use |
|---|---|---|
| `react-route` | `/products/<slug>` | App needs shared auth/credits and is small enough to live in this bundle. Existing AI tools. |
| `static-path` | `/projects/<slug>/` | App is built in its own repo, dropped into `public/projects/<slug>/`. **Default for new apps.** |
| `external-url` | other domain | App lives elsewhere |

**URL canonicalization (enforced by `src/App.tsx`):**
- `/projects/<slug>` (no trailing slash, react-route) → redirects to `/products/<slug>`
- `/app/<old-slug>` → redirects to `/products/<canonical-slug>`
- `/projects/<slug>/` (trailing slash, static-path) → served by Fastify static, never hits the SPA

**Adding a new app from another Claude session:** read [`docs/host-contract.md`](docs/host-contract.md) and use the [`bilko-host` MCP](mcp-host-server/README.md). Don't edit `projectsRegistry.ts` by hand from a sibling repo.

The portfolio (`/`, `/projects`, `⌘K`) reads from `projectsRegistry.ts`, so once registered the app shows up everywhere. (`/products` itself redirects to `/projects`; only `/products/<slug>` paths stay live.) Static-path and external apps trigger a full page load on click (so Fastify serves the static bundle); React routes use SPA navigation.

## Key Architecture

### host-kit (`packages/host-kit/`)
This is the client SDK that static-path siblings use. It provides `authFetch`/`useAuth` (Clerk Bearer auth to the host's `/api`), the games hooks, `SiteHeader`, `GameShell`, and the `bilko-host-kit` manifest CLI. It is a pnpm workspace package with its own build and tests (`pnpm --filter host-kit build|test|typecheck`).

All 14 sibling consumers depend on it locally with `"host-kit": "file:../Bilko/packages/host-kit"`. None of them use npm. Those consumers are the 8 AI-tool pages, Stepproof, Academy, Sudoku, Etch, Fizzpop and MindSwiffer.
- **After changing it:** pnpm copies the untracked `dist/` into each app. Run `pnpm --filter host-kit build` here, then `pnpm install` in each app.
- **Tailwind:** apps that render its components need `@source "<rel>/node_modules/host-kit/dist";` in their Tailwind CSS, because Tailwind skips `node_modules`.
- **Changesets:** add a `.changeset/*.md` (root `.changeset/`) for each change.
- **npm releases:** optional. Push a `host-kit-vX.Y.Z` tag to run `.github/workflows/host-kit-release.yml`. This needs an `NPM_AUTOMATION_TOKEN` repo secret.
- **History:** merged in from `StanislavBG/bilko-host-kit` (now archived) on 2026-10-04, with its full history.

### Shared Hooks (`src/hooks/`)
- `usePageView` — Page view tracking with Clerk email

Clerk auth state comes straight from `@clerk/clerk-react` (`useUser()` / `useAuth()`); there is no host-side `useAuth` wrapper.

### Backend Patterns (`server/`)
- `server/routes/tools/` — One file per AI tool. `_shared.ts` holds the rate limiter, IP hashing, usage tracking, and the shared gateway helpers: `freeTierGate` (free-tier rate limit), `creditGate` (paid credit check/deduct), `askGeminiJson` (Gemini call + JSON parse), `toolErrorReply` (uniform error reply), plus `handleGenerateEndpoint` (inverse-mode generator). `index.ts` is the barrel that registers all tools. To extract a tool to a sibling repo, lift its file + the page; no other server changes required.
- `server/routes/blog.ts` — Blog CRUD (admin-only writes)
- `server/routes/project-catalog.ts` — public `GET /api/projects` + read-only MCP at `/mcp` (the public `/projects` cards as data; contract in `docs/host-contract.md` → "Public project catalog"; card content is project-owned via each registry entry's `listing`, see "Project listing — who owns what")
- `server/routes/stripe.ts` — Checkout, webhooks, billing portal

// Hosted Git Viewer portfolios — gateway for the git-viewer sibling
// (~/Projects/git-viewer). Contract: git-viewer docs/prds/10-hosted-portfolios.md.
//
//   GET  /api/git-viewer/u/:login   public → 200 ready | 202 generating | 404 not_found | 429 rate_limited
//   POST /api/git-viewer/claim      Clerk  → owner (GitHub login linked in Clerk) picks up to 12 repos
//
// Portfolios are generated in-process by the git-viewer library's
// buildPortfolio() with the server's GITHUB_TOKEN, at most 2 at a time, and
// cached in git_viewer_profiles. Free: 3 projects, regenerated at most once per
// 24h when viewed. Paid ($5/mo git_viewer subscription, or a legacy
// pro/business/team plan): up to 12 chosen repos + Writing, refreshed daily.

export const GIT_VIEWER_ENDPOINT = 'git-viewer';
export const LOGIN_RE = /^[A-Za-z0-9](?:[A-Za-z0-9]|-(?=[A-Za-z0-9])){0,38}$/;
const REPO_NAME_RE = /^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,100}$/;
export const PLAN_LIMITS = { free: 3, paid: 12 } as const;

const STALE_SEC = 24 * 60 * 60;
const MAX_CONCURRENT = 2;
const MAX_QUEUED = 50;
const POLL_AFTER_SEC = 5;
const NOT_FOUND_TTL_MS = 60 * 60 * 1000;
const FAILED_TTL_MS = 5 * 60 * 1000;
const MAX_RATE_LIMITED_TTL_MS = 60 * 60 * 1000;
const REFRESH_INTERVAL_MS = 60 * 60 * 1000;
const REFRESH_BATCH = 20;

type Tier = 'free' | 'paid';

export type BuildPortfolio = (opts: {
  user: string;
  token?: string;
  maxProjects: number;
  allowlist?: string[];
  writing: 'none' | 'profile-repo';
}) => Promise<{ data: unknown; lockedCount: number }>;

interface ProfileRow {
  login: string;
  payload: string;
  tier: Tier;
  locked_count: number;
  owner_email: string | null;
  allowlist: string | null;
  updated_at: number;
}

interface Job { tier: Tier; allowlist?: string[] }

// ── Portfolio builder (the git-viewer library) ──────────────────────────────
// Loaded lazily so the host boots, and tests run, without the package; tests
// inject a fake via setPortfolioBuilder. The specifier is a variable so the
// server typechecks before @bilkobibitkov/git-viewer is installed.
const LIB = '@bilkobibitkov/git-viewer';
let builder: BuildPortfolio | null | undefined;

export function setPortfolioBuilder(fn: BuildPortfolio | null | undefined): void {
  builder = fn;
}

async function loadBuilder(): Promise<BuildPortfolio | null> {
  if (builder !== undefined) return builder;
  try {
    const mod = await import(LIB) as { buildPortfolio?: BuildPortfolio };
    builder = mod.buildPortfolio ?? null;
  } catch (err: any) {
    console.error(`[git-viewer] ${LIB} not loadable — hosted portfolios disabled:`, err?.message);
    builder = null;
  }
  return builder;
}

// ── In-process generation queue ─────────────────────────────────────────────
const jobs = new Map<string, Job>();   // queued or running, keyed by login
const pending: string[] = [];
let running = 0;
const notFound = new Map<string, number>(); // login → expiry (ms)
const failed = new Map<string, number>();

/** Test hook: wait for the queue to drain. */
export async function drainGitViewerQueue(): Promise<void> {
  while (jobs.size > 0) await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 5));
}

/** Test hook: forget queue and negative-cache state. */
export function resetGitViewerState(): void {
  jobs.clear();
  pending.length = 0;
  running = 0;
  notFound.clear();
  failed.clear();
}

function isFresh(map: Map<string, number>, login: string): boolean {
  const exp = map.get(login);
  if (exp === undefined) return false;
  if (exp > Date.now()) return true;
  map.delete(login);
  return false;
}

/** Queues a generation. A login already queued keeps one job (latest spec wins). */
function enqueue(login: string, job: Job): boolean {
  if (jobs.has(login)) {
    jobs.set(login, job);
    return true;
  }
  if (pending.length >= MAX_QUEUED) return false;
  jobs.set(login, job);
  pending.push(login);
  pump();
  return true;
}

function pump(): void {
  while (running < MAX_CONCURRENT && pending.length > 0) {
    const login = pending.shift()!;
    const job = jobs.get(login)!;
    running++;
    void generate(login, job).finally(() => {
      running--;
      // A claim/upgrade that landed mid-run replaced the spec: run it again.
      if (jobs.get(login) === job) jobs.delete(login);
      else pending.push(login);
      pump();
    });
  }
}

/**
 * How long to remember a failed generation. A GitHub rate-limit error (Octokit
 * RequestError: 403/429 with x-ratelimit-remaining 0 or retry-after) waits until
 * the budget resets, capped at an hour; anything else retries after 5 minutes.
 */
export function failedTtlMs(err: any, now = Date.now()): number {
  const status = err?.status;
  const headers = err?.response?.headers ?? {};
  if (status !== 403 && status !== 429) return FAILED_TTL_MS;
  const retryAfter = Number(headers['retry-after']);
  if (Number.isFinite(retryAfter) && retryAfter > 0) {
    return Math.min(retryAfter * 1000, MAX_RATE_LIMITED_TTL_MS);
  }
  if (String(headers['x-ratelimit-remaining']) !== '0') return FAILED_TTL_MS;
  const resetMs = Number(headers['x-ratelimit-reset']) * 1000 - now;
  if (!Number.isFinite(resetMs)) return FAILED_TTL_MS;
  return Math.min(Math.max(resetMs, 60_000), MAX_RATE_LIMITED_TTL_MS);
}

async function generate(login: string, job: Job): Promise<void> {
  const build = await loadBuilder();
  if (!build) return;
  const paid = job.tier === 'paid';
  try {
    const { data, lockedCount } = await build({
      user: login,
      token: process.env.GITHUB_TOKEN || undefined,
      maxProjects: paid ? PLAN_LIMITS.paid : PLAN_LIMITS.free,
      allowlist: paid && job.allowlist?.length ? job.allowlist : undefined,
      writing: paid ? 'profile-repo' : 'none',
    });
    await dbRun(
      `INSERT INTO git_viewer_profiles (login, payload, tier, locked_count, updated_at) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
       ON CONFLICT(login) DO UPDATE SET payload = excluded.payload, tier = excluded.tier,
         locked_count = excluded.locked_count, updated_at = excluded.updated_at`,
      login, JSON.stringify(data), job.tier, lockedCount, Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000),
    );
    failed.delete(login);
  } catch (err: any) {
    if (err?.status === 404) {
      notFound.set(login, Date.now() + NOT_FOUND_TTL_MS);
    } else {
      const headers = err?.response?.headers ?? {};
      const ttl = failedTtlMs(err);
      console.error(
        `[git-viewer] generation failed for ${login}: status=${err?.status ?? 'n/a'}` +
        ` ratelimit-remaining=${headers['x-ratelimit-remaining'] ?? 'n/a'}` +
        ` ratelimit-limit=${headers['x-ratelimit-limit'] ?? 'n/a'}` +
        ` token=${process.env.GITHUB_TOKEN ? 'set' : 'unset'} retry-in=${Math.ceil(ttl / 1000)}s:`,
        err?.message ?? err,
      );
      failed.set(login, Date.now() + ttl);
    }
  }
}

/** Boot-time check that GITHUB_TOKEN works: logs the core budget (5000/h when authenticated, 60 when not). */
async function logGitHubRateBudget(): Promise<void> {
  const token = process.env.GITHUB_TOKEN;
  try {
    const res = await fetch('https://api.github.com/rate_limit', {
      headers: { 'user-agent': 'bilko-run', ...(token ? { authorization: `Bearer ${token}` } : {}) },
      signal: AbortSignal.timeout(10_000),
    });
    console.log(
      `[git-viewer] GitHub rate budget: http=${res.status} token=${token ? 'set' : 'unset'}` +
      ` limit=${res.headers.get('x-ratelimit-limit')} remaining=${res.headers.get('x-ratelimit-remaining')}`,
    );
  } catch (err: any) {
    console.error('[git-viewer] GitHub rate budget check failed:', err?.message ?? err);
  }
}

// ── Entitlement ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
async function tierFor(row: Pick<ProfileRow, 'owner_email'> | undefined): Promise<Tier> {
  if (!row?.owner_email) return 'free';
  const sub = await getActiveSubscriptionLive(row.owner_email);
  return sub.gitViewer || sub.isPro ? 'paid' : 'free';
}

function jobFor(row: Pick<ProfileRow, 'allowlist'> | undefined, tier: Tier): Job {
  return { tier, allowlist: row?.allowlist ? JSON.parse(row.allowlist) as string[] : undefined };
}

function secondsToUtcMidnight(): number {
  const now = new Date();
  const midnight = Date.UTC(now.getUTCFullYear(), now.getUTCMonth(), now.getUTCDate() + 1);
  return Math.max(1, Math.ceil((midnight - now.getTime()) / 1000));
}

/** Daily refresh: claimed profiles older than 24h. Paid ones regenerate; lapsed paid ones drop to free. */
export async function runGitViewerRefresh(): Promise<number> {
  const cutoff = Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000) - STALE_SEC;
  const rows = await dbAll<ProfileRow>(
    `SELECT login, tier, owner_email, allowlist FROM git_viewer_profiles
     WHERE owner_email IS NOT NULL AND updated_at < ? ORDER BY updated_at ASC LIMIT ?`,
    cutoff, REFRESH_BATCH,
  );
  let queued = 0;
  for (const row of rows) {
    const tier = await tierFor(row);
    if (tier === 'free' && row.tier === 'free') continue;
    if (enqueue(row.login, jobFor(row, tier))) queued++;
  }
  return queued;
}

const OG_PATH_RE = /^\/projects\/git-viewer\/(?:index\.html)?$/;
const AVATAR_RE = /^https:\/\/avatars\.githubusercontent\.com\/[^\s"'<>]+$/;
const OG_PITCH = 'Your Git, your Résumé';

/**
 * Per-user share card for `/projects/git-viewer/?u=<login>`. Reads the cached
 * portfolio only (never queues a generation); an uncached login gets its own
 * name with the static card image, an invalid one falls through to static meta.
 */
export async function gitViewerOg(path: string, query: URLSearchParams): Promise<OgMeta | null> {
  if (!OG_PATH_RE.test(path)) return null;
  const raw = query.get('u') ?? '';
  if (!LOGIN_RE.test(raw)) return null;
  const login = raw.toLowerCase();
  const row = await dbGet<Pick<ProfileRow, 'payload'>>('SELECT payload FROM git_viewer_profiles WHERE login = ?', login);
  let name = raw;
  let avatar: string | undefined;
  try {
    const dev = row?.payload ? (JSON.parse(row.payload) as { developer?: { name?: unknown; avatarUrl?: unknown } }).developer : undefined;
    if (typeof dev?.name === 'string' && dev.name.trim()) name = dev.name.trim().slice(0, 80);
    if (typeof dev?.avatarUrl === 'string' && AVATAR_RE.test(dev.avatarUrl)) avatar = dev.avatarUrl;
  } catch { /* corrupt payload → login-only card */ }
  return {
    title: `${name} — ${OG_PITCH}`,
    description: `${name}'s GitHub as a portfolio and printable résumé. Make yours free in seconds on bilko.run.`,
    url: `https://bilko.run/projects/git-viewer/?u=${encodeURIComponent(raw)}`,
    image: avatar ?? 'https://bilko.run/og/git-viewer.png',
    ...(avatar ? { card: 'summary' as const } : {}),
  };
}

export function registerGitViewerRoutes(app: FastifyInstance): void {
  app.get('/api/git-viewer/u/:login', async (req, reply) => {
    const raw = (req.params as { login: string }).login;
    if (!LOGIN_RE.test(raw)) return reply.code(404).send({ status: 'not_found' });
    const login = raw.toLowerCase();
    reply.header('cache-control', 'no-store');

    const row = await dbGet<ProfileRow>('SELECT * FROM git_viewer_profiles WHERE login = ?', login);

    if (row?.payload) {
      const stale = row.updated_at < Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000) - STALE_SEC;
      // Claimed free profiles can turn paid between daily refreshes (checkout just
      // completed); the subscription lookup is cached for 5 minutes.
      const tier = row.owner_email && row.tier === 'free' ? await tierFor(row) : row.tier;
      if ((stale || tier !== row.tier) && !jobs.has(login) && !isFresh(failed, login)) {
        enqueue(login, jobFor(row, tier));
      }
      reply.header('cache-control', 'public, max-age=300');
      reply.header('content-type', 'application/json; charset=utf-8');
      // payload is stored JSON — splice it in verbatim rather than re-parsing it.
      return reply.send(
        `{"status":"ready","login":${JSON.stringify(login)},"tier":${JSON.stringify(row.tier)},` +
        `"lockedCount":${Number(row.locked_count)},"updatedAt":${JSON.stringify(new Date(row.updated_at * 1000).toISOString())},` +
        `"data":${row.payload}}`,
      );
    }

    if (isFresh(notFound, login)) return reply.code(404).send({ status: 'not_found' });
    if (jobs.has(login)) return reply.code(202).send({ status: 'generating', retryAfterSec: POLL_AFTER_SEC });
    if (isFresh(failed, login)) {
      const retryAfterSec = Math.max(1, Math.ceil((failed.get(login)! - Date.now()) / 1000));
      return reply.code(503).send({ status: 'error', retryAfterSec });
    }
    if (!(await loadBuilder())) return reply.code(503).send({ status: 'unavailable' });

    // Only a NEW generation costs GitHub calls, so only that counts against the IP.
    const ipHash = hashIp(req.ip);
    const rate = await checkRateLimit(ipHash, GIT_VIEWER_ENDPOINT);
    if (!rate.allowed) {
      return reply.code(429).send({ status: 'rate_limited', retryAfterSec: secondsToUtcMidnight() });
    }
    if (!enqueue(login, jobFor(row, await tierFor(row)))) {
      return reply.code(429).send({ status: 'rate_limited', retryAfterSec: 60 });
    }
    await incrementUsage(ipHash, GIT_VIEWER_ENDPOINT);
    return reply.code(202).send({ status: 'generating', retryAfterSec: POLL_AFTER_SEC });
  });

  app.post('/api/git-viewer/claim', async (req, reply) => {
    const body = req.body as { login?: unknown; allowlist?: unknown } | null;
    const raw = typeof body?.login === 'string' ? body.login : '';
    if (!LOGIN_RE.test(raw)) return reply.code(400).send({ error: 'Invalid GitHub login.' });
    const login = raw.toLowerCase();

    const allowlist = body?.allowlist ?? [];
    if (
      !Array.isArray(allowlist) || allowlist.length > PLAN_LIMITS.paid ||
      !allowlist.every(n => typeof n === 'string' && REPO_NAME_RE.test(n))
    ) {
      return reply.code(400).send({ error: `allowlist must be up to ${PLAN_LIMITS.paid} repo names.` });
    }

    const user = await verifyClerkGitHubUser(req.headers.authorization);
    if (!user) return reply.code(401).send({ error: 'Sign in required.' });
    if (!user.githubLogins.includes(login)) {
      return reply.code(403).send({ error: 'Your signed-in account is not linked to this GitHub login.' });
    }

    const allowlistJson = allowlist.length ? JSON.stringify(allowlist) : null;
    await dbRun(
      `INSERT INTO git_viewer_profiles (login, payload, tier, locked_count, owner_email, allowlist, updated_at)
       VALUES (?, '', 'free', 0, ?, ?, 0)
       ON CONFLICT(login) DO UPDATE SET owner_email = excluded.owner_email, allowlist = excluded.allowlist`,
      login, user.email, allowlistJson,
    );
    const tier = await tierFor({ owner_email: user.email });
    enqueue(login, jobFor({ allowlist: allowlistJson }, tier));
    return reply.send({ ok: true, login, tier, allowlist });
  });

  if (!process.env.VITEST) {
    void logGitHubRateBudget();
    const timer = setInterval(() => {
      runGitViewerRefresh().catch(err => console.error('[git-viewer] refresh failed:', err));
    }, REFRESH_INTERVAL_MS);
    timer.unref();
    app.addHook('onClose', async () => clearInterval(timer));
  }
}

export function hashIp(ip: string): string {
  return createHash('sha256').update(ip).digest('hex');
}

export function todayUTC(): string {
  return new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 10);
}

export async function getUsageCount(ipHash: string, endpoint: string): Promise<number> {
  const row = await dbGet<{ count: number }>(
    'SELECT count FROM usage_tracking WHERE ip_hash = ? AND endpoint = ? AND date = ?',
    ipHash, endpoint, todayUTC(),
  );
  return row?.count ?? 0;
}

export async function incrementUsage(ipHash: string, endpoint: string): Promise<number> {
  const row = await dbGet<{ count: number }>(
    `INSERT INTO usage_tracking (ip_hash, endpoint, date, count) VALUES (?, ?, ?, 1) ON CONFLICT(ip_hash, endpoint, date) DO UPDATE SET count = count + 1 RETURNING count`,
    ipHash, endpoint, todayUTC(),
  );
  return row?.count ?? 1;
}

export interface RateLimitResult {
  allowed: boolean;
  remaining: number;
  limit: number;
  isPro: boolean;
}

export function recordFunnelEvent(event: string, ipHash: string, tool?: string, email?: string): void {
  dbRun('INSERT INTO funnel_events (event, ip_hash, tool, email) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)', event, ipHash, tool ?? null, email ?? null).catch(() => {});
}

export async function checkRateLimit(ipHash: string, endpoint: string, email?: string, productKey?: string): Promise<RateLimitResult> {
  if (email) {
    if (productKey && await hasPurchased(email, productKey)) {
      const count = await getUsageCount(ipHash, endpoint);
      const limit = PAID_TIER_LIMIT;
      if (count >= limit) return { allowed: false, remaining: 0, limit, isPro: true };
      return { allowed: true, remaining: limit - count, limit, isPro: true };
    }
    const sub = await getActiveSubscriptionLive(email);
    if (sub.isPro) {
      const limit = TIER_LIMITS[sub.tier] || PAID_TIER_LIMIT;
      const count = await getUsageCount(ipHash, endpoint);
      if (count >= limit) return { allowed: false, remaining: 0, limit, isPro: true };
      return { allowed: true, remaining: limit - count, limit, isPro: true };
    }
  }
  const count = await getUsageCount(ipHash, endpoint);
  if (count >= FREE_TIER_LIMIT) {
    recordFunnelEvent('free_limit_hit', ipHash, endpoint, email);
    return { allowed: false, remaining: 0, limit: FREE_TIER_LIMIT, isPro: false };
  }
  return { allowed: true, remaining: FREE_TIER_LIMIT - count, limit: FREE_TIER_LIMIT, isPro: false };
}

async function getCeiling(appSlug: string): Promise<number | null> {
  const hit = ceilingCache.get(appSlug);
  if (hit && hit.expires > Date.now()) return hit.value;
  const row = await dbGet<{ max_calls_per_day: number }>(

  );
  const value = row?.max_calls_per_day ?? null;
  if (ceilingTtlMs > 0) ceilingCache.set(appSlug, { value, expires: Date.now() + ceilingTtlMs });
  return value;

  if (builder !== undefined) return builder;

// ── In-process generation queue ─────────────────────────────────────────────
const jobs = new Map<string, Job>();   // queued or running, keyed by login
const pending: string[] = [];
let running = 0;
const notFound = new Map<string, number>(); // login → expiry (ms)
const failed = new Map<string, number>();

/** Test hook: wait for the queue to drain. */
export async function drainGitViewerQueue(): Promise<void> {
  while (jobs.size > 0) await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 5));
}

/** Test hook: forget queue and negative-cache state. */
export function resetGitViewerState(): void {
  jobs.clear();
  pending.length = 0;
  running = 0;
  notFound.clear();
  failed.clear();
}

function isFresh(map: Map<string, number>, login: string): boolean {
  const exp = map.get(login);
  if (exp === undefined) return false;
  if (exp > Date.now()) return true;
  map.delete(login);
  return false;
}

/** Queues a generation. A login already queued keeps one job (latest spec wins). */
function enqueue(login: string, job: Job): boolean {
  if (jobs.has(login)) {
    jobs.set(login, job);
    return true;
  }
  if (pending.length >= MAX_QUEUED) return false;
  jobs.set(login, job);
  pending.push(login);
  pump();
  return true;
}

function pump(): void {
  while (running < MAX_CONCURRENT && pending.length > 0) {
    const login = pending.shift()!;
    const job = jobs.get(login)!;
    running++;
    void generate(login, job).finally(() => {
      running--;
      // A claim/upgrade that landed mid-run replaced the spec: run it again.
      if (jobs.get(login) === job) jobs.delete(login);
      else pending.push(login);
      pump();
    });
  }
}

/**
 * How long to remember a failed generation. A GitHub rate-limit error (Octokit
 * RequestError: 403/429 with x-ratelimit-remaining 0 or retry-after) waits until
 * the budget resets, capped at an hour; anything else retries after 5 minutes.
 */
export function failedTtlMs(err: any, now = Date.now()): number {
  const status = err?.status;
  const headers = err?.response?.headers ?? {};
  if (status !== 403 && status !== 429) return FAILED_TTL_MS;
  const retryAfter = Number(headers['retry-after']);
  if (Number.isFinite(retryAfter) && retryAfter > 0) {
    return Math.min(retryAfter * 1000, MAX_RATE_LIMITED_TTL_MS);
  }
  if (String(headers['x-ratelimit-remaining']) !== '0') return FAILED_TTL_MS;
  const resetMs = Number(headers['x-ratelimit-reset']) * 1000 - now;
  if (!Number.isFinite(resetMs)) return FAILED_TTL_MS;
  return Math.min(Math.max(resetMs, 60_000), MAX_RATE_LIMITED_TTL_MS);
}

async function generate(login: string, job: Job): Promise<void> {
  const build = await loadBuilder();
  if (!build) return;
  const paid = job.tier === 'paid';
  try {
    const { data, lockedCount } = await build({
      user: login,
      token: process.env.GITHUB_TOKEN || undefined,
      maxProjects: paid ? PLAN_LIMITS.paid : PLAN_LIMITS.free,
      allowlist: paid && job.allowlist?.length ? job.allowlist : undefined,
      writing: paid ? 'profile-repo' : 'none',
    });
    await dbRun(
      `INSERT INTO git_viewer_profiles (login, payload, tier, locked_count, updated_at) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
       ON CONFLICT(login) DO UPDATE SET payload = excluded.payload, tier = excluded.tier,
         locked_count = excluded.locked_count, updated_at = excluded.updated_at`,
      login, JSON.stringify(data), job.tier, lockedCount, Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000),
    );
    failed.delete(login);
  } catch (err: any) {
    if (err?.status === 404) {
      notFound.set(login, Date.now() + NOT_FOUND_TTL_MS);
    } else {
      const headers = err?.response?.headers ?? {};
      const ttl = failedTtlMs(err);
      console.error(
        `[git-viewer] generation failed for ${login}: status=${err?.status ?? 'n/a'}` +
        ` ratelimit-remaining=${headers['x-ratelimit-remaining'] ?? 'n/a'}` +
        ` ratelimit-limit=${headers['x-ratelimit-limit'] ?? 'n/a'}` +
        ` token=${process.env.GITHUB_TOKEN ? 'set' : 'unset'} retry-in=${Math.ceil(ttl / 1000)}s:`,
        err?.message ?? err,
      );
      failed.set(login, Date.now() + ttl);
    }
  }
}

/** Boot-time check that GITHUB_TOKEN works: logs the core budget (5000/h when authenticated, 60 when not). */

async function tierFor(row: Pick<ProfileRow, 'owner_email'> | undefined): Promise<Tier> {
  if (!row?.owner_email) return 'free';
  const sub = await getActiveSubscriptionLive(row.owner_email);
  return sub.gitViewer || sub.isPro ? 'paid' : 'free';
}

function jobFor(row: Pick<ProfileRow, 'allowlist'> | undefined, tier: Tier): Job {
  return { tier, allowlist: row?.allowlist ? JSON.parse(row.allowlist) as string[] : undefined };
}

function secondsToUtcMidnight(): number {
  const now = new Date();
  const midnight = Date.UTC(now.getUTCFullYear(), now.getUTCMonth(), now.getUTCDate() + 1);
  return Math.max(1, Math.ceil((midnight - now.getTime()) / 1000));
}

/** Daily refresh: claimed profiles older than 24h. Paid ones regenerate; lapsed paid ones drop to free. */
export async function runGitViewerRefresh(): Promise<number> {
  const cutoff = Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000) - STALE_SEC;
  const rows = await dbAll<ProfileRow>(
    `SELECT login, tier, owner_email, allowlist FROM git_viewer_profiles
     WHERE owner_email IS NOT NULL AND updated_at < ? ORDER BY updated_at ASC LIMIT ?`,
    cutoff, REFRESH_BATCH,
  );
  let queued = 0;
  for (const row of rows) {
    const tier = await tierFor(row);
    if (tier === 'free' && row.tier === 'free') continue;
    if (enqueue(row.login, jobFor(row, tier))) queued++;
  }
  return queued;
}

const OG_PATH_RE = /^\/projects\/git-viewer\/(?:index\.html)?$/;
const AVATAR_RE = /^https:\/\/avatars\.githubusercontent\.com\/[^\s"'<>]+$/;
const OG_PITCH = 'Your Git, your Résumé';

/**
 * Per-user share card for `/projects/git-viewer/?u=<login>`. Reads the cached

 * name with the static card image, an invalid one falls through to static meta.

export async function gitViewerOg(path: string, query: URLSearchParams): Promise<OgMeta | null> {
  if (!OG_PATH_RE.test(path)) return null;
  const raw = query.get('u') ?? '';
  if (!LOGIN_RE.test(raw)) return null;
  const login = raw.toLowerCase();
  const row = await dbGet<Pick<ProfileRow, 'payload'>>('SELECT payload FROM git_viewer_profiles WHERE login = ?', login);
  let name = raw;
  let avatar: string | undefined;
  try {
    const dev = row?.payload ? (JSON.parse(row.payload) as { developer?: { name?: unknown; avatarUrl?: unknown } }).developer : undefined;
    if (typeof dev?.name === 'string' && dev.name.trim()) name = dev.name.trim().slice(0, 80);
    if (typeof dev?.avatarUrl === 'string' && AVATAR_RE.test(dev.avatarUrl)) avatar = dev.avatarUrl;
  } catch { /* corrupt payload → login-only card */ }
  return {
    title: `${name} — ${OG_PITCH}`,
    description: `${name}'s GitHub as a portfolio and printable résumé. Make yours free in seconds on bilko.run.`,
    url: `https://bilko.run/projects/git-viewer/?u=${encodeURIComponent(raw)}`,
    image: avatar ?? 'https://bilko.run/og/git-viewer.png',
    ...(avatar ? { card: 'summary' as const } : {}),
  };
}

export function registerGitViewerRoutes(app: FastifyInstance): void {
  app.get('/api/git-viewer/u/:login', async (req, reply) => {
    const raw = (req.params as { login: string }).login;
    if (!LOGIN_RE.test(raw)) return reply.code(404).send({ status: 'not_found' });
    const login = raw.toLowerCase();
    reply.header('cache-control', 'no-store');

    const row = await dbGet<ProfileRow>('SELECT * FROM git_viewer_profiles WHERE login = ?', login);

    if (row?.payload) {
      const stale = row.updated_at < Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000) - STALE_SEC;
      // Claimed free profiles can turn paid between daily refreshes (checkout just
      // completed); the subscription lookup is cached for 5 minutes.
      const tier = row.owner_email && row.tier === 'free' ? await tierFor(row) : row.tier;
      if ((stale || tier !== row.tier) && !jobs.has(login) && !isFresh(failed, login)) {
        enqueue(login, jobFor(row, tier));
      }
      reply.header('cache-control', 'public, max-age=300');
      reply.header('content-type', 'application/json; charset=utf-8');
      // payload is stored JSON — splice it in verbatim rather than re-parsing it.
      return reply.send(
        `{"status":"ready","login":${JSON.stringify(login)},"tier":${JSON.stringify(row.tier)},` +
        `"lockedCount":${Number(row.locked_count)},"updatedAt":${JSON.stringify(new Date(row.updated_at * 1000).toISOString())},` +
        `"data":${row.payload}}`,
      );
    }

    if (isFresh(notFound, login)) return reply.code(404).send({ status: 'not_found' });
    if (jobs.has(login)) return reply.code(202).send({ status: 'generating', retryAfterSec: POLL_AFTER_SEC });
    if (isFresh(failed, login)) {
      const retryAfterSec = Math.max(1, Math.ceil((failed.get(login)! - Date.now()) / 1000));
      return reply.code(503).send({ status: 'error', retryAfterSec });
    }
    if (!(await loadBuilder())) return reply.code(503).send({ status: 'unavailable' });

    // Only a NEW generation costs GitHub calls, so only that counts against the IP.
    const ipHash = hashIp(req.ip);
    const rate = await checkRateLimit(ipHash, GIT_VIEWER_ENDPOINT);
    if (!rate.allowed) {
      return reply.code(429).send({ status: 'rate_limited', retryAfterSec: secondsToUtcMidnight() });
    }
    if (!enqueue(login, jobFor(row, await tierFor(row)))) {
      return reply.code(429).send({ status: 'rate_limited', retryAfterSec: 60 });
    }
    await incrementUsage(ipHash, GIT_VIEWER_ENDPOINT);
    return reply.code(202).send({ status: 'generating', retryAfterSec: POLL_AFTER_SEC });
  });

  app.post('/api/git-viewer/claim', async (req, reply) => {
    const body = req.body as { login?: unknown; allowlist?: unknown } | null;
    const raw = typeof body?.login === 'string' ? body.login : '';
    if (!LOGIN_RE.test(raw)) return reply.code(400).send({ error: 'Invalid GitHub login.' });
    const login = raw.toLowerCase();

    const allowlist = body?.allowlist ?? [];
    if (
      !Array.isArray(allowlist) || allowlist.length > PLAN_LIMITS.paid ||
      !allowlist.every(n => typeof n === 'string' && REPO_NAME_RE.test(n))
    ) {
      return reply.code(400).send({ error: `allowlist must be up to ${PLAN_LIMITS.paid} repo names.` });
    }

    const user = await verifyClerkGitHubUser(req.headers.authorization);
    if (!user) return reply.code(401).send({ error: 'Sign in required.' });
    if (!user.githubLogins.includes(login)) {
      return reply.code(403).send({ error: 'Your signed-in account is not linked to this GitHub login.' });
    }

    const allowlistJson = allowlist.length ? JSON.stringify(allowlist) : null;
    await dbRun(
      `INSERT INTO git_viewer_profiles (login, payload, tier, locked_count, owner_email, allowlist, updated_at)
       VALUES (?, '', 'free', 0, ?, ?, 0)
       ON CONFLICT(login) DO UPDATE SET owner_email = excluded.owner_email, allowlist = excluded.allowlist`,
      login, user.email, allowlistJson,
    );
    const tier = await tierFor({ owner_email: user.email });
    enqueue(login, jobFor({ allowlist: allowlistJson }, tier));
    return reply.send({ ok: true, login, tier, allowlist });
  });

  if (!process.env.VITEST) {
    void logGitHubRateBudget();
    const timer = setInterval(() => {
      runGitViewerRefresh().catch(err => console.error('[git-viewer] refresh failed:', err));
    }, REFRESH_INTERVAL_MS);
    timer.unref();
    app.addHook('onClose', async () => clearInterval(timer));
  }
}

export interface RateLimitResult {
  allowed: boolean;
  remaining: number;
  limit: number;
  isPro: boolean;
}

export function recordFunnelEvent(event: string, ipHash: string, tool?: string, email?: string): void {
  dbRun('INSERT INTO funnel_events (event, ip_hash, tool, email) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)', event, ipHash, tool ?? null, email ?? null).catch(() => {});
}

export async function checkRateLimit(ipHash: string, endpoint: string, email?: string, productKey?: string): Promise<RateLimitResult> {
  if (email) {
    if (productKey && await hasPurchased(email, productKey)) {
      const count = await getUsageCount(ipHash, endpoint);
      const limit = PAID_TIER_LIMIT;
      if (count >= limit) return { allowed: false, remaining: 0, limit, isPro: true };
      return { allowed: true, remaining: limit - count, limit, isPro: true };
    }
    const sub = await getActiveSubscriptionLive(email);
    if (sub.isPro) {
      const limit = TIER_LIMITS[sub.tier] || PAID_TIER_LIMIT;
      const count = await getUsageCount(ipHash, endpoint);
      if (count >= limit) return { allowed: false, remaining: 0, limit, isPro: true };
      return { allowed: true, remaining: limit - count, limit, isPro: true };
    }
  }
  const count = await getUsageCount(ipHash, endpoint);
  if (count >= FREE_TIER_LIMIT) {
    recordFunnelEvent('free_limit_hit', ipHash, endpoint, email);
    return { allowed: false, remaining: 0, limit: FREE_TIER_LIMIT, isPro: false };
  }
  return { allowed: true, remaining: FREE_TIER_LIMIT - count, limit: FREE_TIER_LIMIT, isPro: false };
}

The `execute_blender_code` tool runs Python code via `bpy` in the connected Blender instance.

The `execute_blender_code` tool is a last resort, if there are other tools that provide

# Scene & Data Structure

Blender uses a datablock system - objects and their underlying data (meshes, materials,
cameras, etc.) are separate entities.

Hierarchy:
  * **Scene** - top-level container. A .blend can have multiple.
  * **View Layer** - controls collection visibility/selectability.
  * **Collection** - organizational tree. Objects live in collections; can be nested;
    objects can belong to multiple collections.
  * **Object** - has a transform (location, rotation, scale) and references underlying data
    (Mesh, Curve, Camera, etc.). Multiple objects can share the same data (linked duplicates).
  * **Datablocks** - the actual data: geometry, materials, textures, etc.

Key concepts:
  * Objects and data are separate - deleting one does not delete the other.
  * Orphaned datablocks (zero users) are purged on save/reload or manual purge.
  * Objects created via the data API must be linked to a collection to appear in a scene.
  * Shared data: check user count before modifying a datablock - editing a shared mesh
    affects all objects referencing it. Make single-user first if needed.
  * In most cases file assets:
    * Images, Fonts, Sounds, other `.blend` files -  corraspond to a data-block.

Visibility has three independent states:
  * **Viewport hidden** - still fully scriptable.
  * **Disabled in view layer** - excluded; may be inaccessible to view-layer-dependent operators.
  * **Disabled for render** - skipped during render, otherwise normal.
Check these when objects seem "missing" or operators skip them.

Blender defaults to meters. Check scene unit settings before creating dimensioned objects.

Exploring scenes:
  * Walk the collection hierarchy for an overview first.
  * Don't dump entire scenes - inspect progressively for large scenes.
  * Check object types, parenting, modifiers, and materials before making changes.

describe('POST /api/git-viewer/claim', () => {
  it('401 without a verified Clerk user', async () => {
    expect((await claim({ login: 'octocat' })).statusCode).toBe(401);
  });

  it('403 when the linked GitHub login does not match', async () => {
    vi.mocked(verifyClerkGitHubUser).mockResolvedValue({ email: 'a@x.com', githubLogins: ['someone-else'] });
    const res = await claim({ login: 'octocat' });
    expect(res.statusCode).toBe(403);
    expect(await dbGet('SELECT login FROM git_viewer_profiles WHERE login = ?', 'octocat')).toBeUndefined();
  });

  it('400 for more than 12 repos', async () => {
    vi.mocked(verifyClerkGitHubUser).mockResolvedValue({ email: 'a@x.com', githubLogins: ['octocat'] });
    const res = await claim({ login: 'octocat', allowlist: Array.from({ length: 13 }, (_, i) => `r${i}`) });
    expect(res.statusCode).toBe(400);
  });

  it('a git_viewer subscriber gets paid: 12 chosen repos + Writing', async () => {
    vi.mocked(verifyClerkGitHubUser).mockResolvedValue({ email: 'a@x.com', githubLogins: ['octocat'] });
    vi.mocked(getActiveSubscriptionLive).mockResolvedValue({ isPro: false, tier: 'free', gitViewer: true });
    const res = await claim({ login: 'OctoCat', allowlist: ['hello-world', 'Spoon-Knife'] });
    expect(res.statusCode).toBe(200);
    expect(res.json()).toMatchObject({ ok: true, login: 'octocat', tier: 'paid' });
    await drainGitViewerQueue();
    expect(build).toHaveBeenCalledWith(expect.objectContaining({
      user: 'octocat', maxProjects: PLAN_LIMITS.paid, allowlist: ['hello-world', 'Spoon-Knife'], writing: 'profile-repo',
    }));
    const ready = (await get('octocat')).json();
    expect(ready.tier).toBe('paid');
    expect(ready.data.projects).toHaveLength(12);
  });

  it('a legacy pro subscriber gets paid included', async () => {
    vi.mocked(verifyClerkGitHubUser).mockResolvedValue({ email: 'p@x.com', githubLogins: ['octocat'] });
    vi.mocked(getActiveSubscriptionLive).mockResolvedValue({ isPro: true, tier: 'pro', gitViewer: false });
    expect((await claim({ login: 'octocat' })).json().tier).toBe('paid');
  });

  it('a claimed free profile without a subscription stays free', async () => {
    vi.mocked(verifyClerkGitHubUser).mockResolvedValue({ email: 'a@x.com', githubLogins: ['octocat'] });
    expect((await claim({ login: 'octocat', allowlist: ['a'] })).json().tier).toBe('free');
    await drainGitViewerQueue();
    expect(build).toHaveBeenCalledWith(expect.objectContaining({ maxProjects: PLAN_LIMITS.free, allowlist: undefined }));
  });
});
